Why you need it

Why Businesses and Landlords in Bay Shore Use Master Key Systems

A building with a dozen doors and a dozen key rings is a management problem: managers carrying a pocketful of keys, staff sharing copies, and no record of who can open what. A master key system fixes that. Each person gets one key that opens exactly the doors they should, and a master key opens them all. Businesses, medical offices, multi-tenant buildings, and landlords with several units in Bay Shore use these systems to control access without carrying dozens of keys.

Local note · Bay Shore

Drivers who leave cars near the Bay Shore ferry terminals for the day sometimes return to a dead key fob or keys locked inside, and salt air near the bay is also hard on exterior locks.

How we do it

How We Design and Install a Master Key System in Bay Shore

We walk the building, count the doors, and map who needs access to what. From that we design a hierarchy: individual keys for each door, sub-master keys for departments or floors, and a grand master for management. We then rekey your existing locks to the system, or replace locks that cannot be rekeyed, and cut the keys. Restricted keyways can be added so keys cannot be duplicated at a hardware store without authorization. We keep a key record so future locks and keys can be added to the same system.

Cost & lifespan

Master Key System Cost in Bay Shore and What Drives It

A master key system in Bay Shore typically runs $150 and up, depending on the number of locks, driven mainly by the number of locks, the number of key levels, and whether restricted keyways are used. Rekeying existing locks is far cheaper than replacing them, so we start there. Once installed, the system lasts as long as the locks themselves, and expanding it later costs much less than starting over. We give a flat quote after a walk-through.

If you wait

What Happens When Keys Are Not Controlled

When employees, tenants, and contractors all carry unmanaged copies, you lose track of who can get into the building, and rekeying everything after each departure gets expensive. A lost key can mean changing the whole building rather than one lock. A system built around a controlled key hierarchy limits the fallout when a key goes missing. Business owners in Bay Shore and nearby Brightwaters and West Islip who set it up early avoid the costly rekey-everything cycle.
